papers.title: FoxO1 and HNF1α cooperatively remodel nucleosome architecture and mechanical stability to activate transcription
papers.abstract: How different transcription factors (TFs) cooperate to bind nucleosomal DNA targets remains unclear. Cryo-EM and force spectroscopy show that the pioneer factor FoxO1 binds superhelical location (SHL) +2 of nucleosomes assembled on the human IGFBP1 promoter, enhances distal DNA unwrapping, destabilizes the histone core, and reduces nucleosome mechanical stability. TF HNF1 binds SHL +5/+7 as a dimer, induces extensive DNA unwrapping without perturbing the histone core, and reshapes nucleosome disassembly dynamics. FoxO1 enhances HNF1 recruitment, and together they stabilize the nucleosome during its mechanically-induced disassembly trajectories. In-cell nucleosome footprinting on active promoters shows that FoxO1 binding enhances unwrapped nucleosomes and subnucleosomes presence, while HNF1 increases stabilized and breathing nucleosomes and reduces the subnucleosome population. Combined, they display an intermediate nucleosome phenotype. Our data leads to a model where FoxO1 destabilizes the nucleosome and enhances HNF1 recruitment, and together they remodel nucleosome architecture both in vitro and in native chromatin.

papers.title: Particle picking and centering in cryo-electron micrographs via a vanishing radial kernel
papers.abstract: A training-free procedure combines particle picking and approximate centering in cryo-electron microscopy through a single convolution of the micrograph with a compact radial kernel, whose weights increase with distance from the origin, saturate in an annulus, and vanish beyond it. Particles are darker than their surroundings and much weaker than the noise; each carves a well in the response, and local minima of the response are candidate centers. Constant background offsets leave these extrema unchanged away from image boundaries, and a local stability bound controls the displacement of a well's minimum under signed perturbations without assuming a symmetric particle. Grid seeds are iteratively updated, nearby endpoints are merged, and two-dimensional classification follows. On the emph{Plasmodium falciparum} 80S ribosome and $beta$-galactosidase data sets, reconstructions reach 3.68 and 4.30~AA{}, compared with 3.77 and 4.36~AA{} using reference coordinates, with picking at 0.20--0.26~s per micrograph.

papers.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models
papers.abstract: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase domain. Across both mutational effect prediction and drug-target affinity tasks, current AI models produce largely ligand-invariant predictions despite experimentally distinct inhibitor-dependent fitness landscapes. Ligand-aware geometric models, including LigandMPNN and LASErMPNN, partially recover experimentally validated resistance-associated hotspots, highlighting the importance of explicitly modeling protein-ligand interactions and local structural flexibility. In contrast, deep learning affinity prediction models underestimate mutation-induced changes in binding affinity. This deficiency likely reflects mutation-invariant structural priors derived from co-folded structure prediction frameworks and the absence of mutation-conditioned supervision in current affinity datasets. Finally, we further extended our analysis to several kinase-inhibitor deep mutational scanning datasets and confirm the overall trends. Our findings suggest that a primary limitation in improving performance on this task lies in the scarcity of mutation-conditioned protein-ligand training data rather than model architecture alone.

papers.title: Comparative cryo-EM structures of CGMMV and ToMMV reveal divergent coat protein packing and electrostatics indicating Tobamovirus host specificity
papers.abstract: Tobamoviruses are a group of economically important plant viruses exhibiting extreme stability and persistence. Despite high morphological similarity, they show extensive host-family specificity, cause a range of symptoms, and cause significant global yield loss in fruit and vegetable plants. Composed of a rod-shaped helical assembly of identical coat proteins encasing a single-stranded RNA, Tobamoviruses have long served as fundamental models for understanding helical assemblies. Here we report the cryo-EM structures of two viruses from this genus, CGMMV and ToMMV, at 2.86 [A] and 2.71 [A] resolution, respectively. The structures reveal divergent packing strategies within the virion assembly. While ToMMV is genetically similar to the canonical Tobamovirus TMV and displays a structure closely resembling TMV, CGMMV employs a more hydrophobic packing strategy, particularly in the solvent-exposed inner loop region of the coat protein. Comparative biophysical and molecular dynamics analyses from the reconstructed structures reveal more stable and compact protein packing for CGMMV at both the subunit and assembly levels. Furthermore, this study reports a newly identified electrostatic patch existing at the lower alpha-helix region of the coat protein that serves as an additional RNA-stabilizing region, with host family-specific amino acid substitutions among Tobamoviruses. Our study elucidates the structural mechanics and evolutionary strategies driving virion stability and host diversity while maintaining a conserved helical assembly. These findings reveal how subtle electrostatic tuning and divergent packing strategies drive viral stability and host adaptation within a strictly conserved quaternary scaffold.

papers.title: Bottom-heaviness stabilizes pelagic fish eggs and generates advective transport at their surface
papers.abstract: Pelagic fish eggs are small spheres (~1 mm) that drift in the open ocean, carried by large-scale currents. Embedded in these currents are egg-scale turbulent eddies that impose local rotational forcing on the eggs. Accordingly, eggs are considered passive tracer particles that move with these eddies, implying that mass transfer of oxygen and waste are controlled only by molecular diffusion. However, eggs are bottom heavy, characterized by a dense embryo and a buoyant oil globule at opposing poles. We hypothesized that such internal structure generates a gravitational restoring torque, stabilizing the egg and generating relative egg-water motion. To test this hypothesis we exposed fish eggs to controlled flows with shear levels typical of upper mixed-layer and estuarine environments, and analyzed their dynamics. Eggs displayed one of two repeatable behaviors: (i) steady orientation, with a near-constant egg angle, and (ii) revolving motion, with egg rotation at time-varying angular speed. Both behaviors generated relative motion between the eggs and the surrounding water. A rigid-body rotational model balancing external flow-induced torque and gravitational restoring torque showed that transitions between these states depend on local flow fields and developmental stage, with older eggs shifting to revolving behavior at lower external fluid torque. Together, these findings suggest that advective transport is important and that diffusion-only models underestimate exchange rates, which are a major component in predicting the effects of environmental factors on embryo survival.

papers.title: End-to-end reconstruction for cryo electron ptychographic single-particle analysis
papers.abstract: Cryo-electron ptychographic (cryo-ptycho) single-particle analysis (SPA) is a diffractive imaging method for protein structure determination. Current reconstruction workflows sequentially reconstruct a 2D phase micrograph from each scan, and then apply conventional SPA software to the resulting projections to obtain a 3D potential map. Here, we introduce End2EndPtychoSPA, an end-to-end reconstruction algorithm that directly fits a 3D electrostatic potential volume and particle poses to 4D-STEM diffraction data using a differentiable multislice forward model. On simulated haemoglobin data where the sequential route recovers initial poses, End2EndPtychoSPA with a learnable vitreous-ice layer reaches 3.22 A resolution against the ground truth (FSC 0.5), compared with 3.41 A for the sequential route. We also compare End2EndPtychoSPA with the sequential route on four published experimental cryo-ptycho SPA datasets. On apoferritin (11,552 particles), the End2EndPtychoSPA map improves agreement with an external atomic model over both our matched sequential route on the same particles and the deposited EMD-19425 half-map mean, and shifts the unmasked half-map FSC 0.143 crossing from 6.83 A to 5.99 A. On T20S, TMV and Phi92, End2EndPtychoSPA does not yet improve upon the 2D route.

papers.title: Beyond Direct Binding: Serotonin Rewires Model Brain Plasma Membrane-Mediated Communication Pathways in Y4R
papers.abstract: Serotonin, an endogenous neurotransmitter, modulates pancreatic polypeptide (PP) recognition by the neuropeptide Y4 receptor (Y4R), a mechanism relevant to altered serotonergic signaling associated with metabolic disorder and anxiety. Although recent experiment demonstrates serotonin modulated PP dissociation kinetics of Y4R through membrane allostery, the molecular mechanism of serotonin induced lipidomic reorganization of the brain plasma membrane (BPM) relevant for Y4R activation is unknown. To this end, a total of 825.9 ns long all atom molecular dynamics simulations at 310 K elucidate the concentration-dependent coupling between serotonin partitioning, selective lipid reorganization, and PP binding and Y4R activation relevant intra-receptor communication in a heterogeneous, asymmetric model BPM. In the absence of serotonin, Y4R preferentially associates with the anionic lipids. Serotonin preferentially localizes at the lipid water interface over the PP binding and activation-associated regions of Y4R. At 6 mM, serotonin preferentially contacts phosphocholine species depleted from Y4R, whereas at 50 mM, phosphatidylinositol 4,5 bisphosphate dominates both microenvironments. These changes align with the selective remodeling of lipid networks, enhanced lipid chain ordering, and modest bilayer compaction. Weighted implementation of suboptimal paths analysis reveals concentration-dependent reorganization of communication pathways between experimentally implicated PP binding and activation associated Y4R residues. Collectively, these findings connects serotonin dependent selective lipid redistribution to altered intramolecular communication between Y4R residues associated with PP binding and G-protein coupling, and provide a framework for future experiments investigating membrane-mediated neuromodulation and neuronal signaling. These findings provide a basis for exploring lipid-targeted pharmacology as a complementary strategy to modulate GPCR allostery by altering membrane composition rather than directly targeting the receptor.

papers.title: Ultra-precision 3D Printed Sample Tubes of Complex Cross Section for Enhanced Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Sensitivity of AqueousSamples
papers.abstract: This paper discusses the applications of ultra-precision 3D printing in developing EPR sample tubes for X-band measurements of aqueous samples. The seed idea of this work started from the flat cell idea discussed in Mett and Hyde et al.(2003), Sidabras et al. (2005), and Sidabras et al. (2017), where placing multiple aqueous flat cells perpendicular to the electric field in the microwave cavity reduce RF losses and improve EPR signal sensitivity. In this work, we present the 3D printed aquastar sample holders for dielectric resonators and the aquasun sample holders for cavity resonators. Even though the ultra-precision 3D printing enables the fabrication of complex cross-sections at 25um resolution, the photopolymer material has comparatively higher dielectric losses compared to the conventional materials like glass and PTFE. To reduce the RF losses due to the inherent dielectric properties, we introduced the latticing approach in reducing the amount of plastic without compromising the structural stability. In addition to this, we present the slicing and dielectric approximation approach in reducing the computation cost for these complex cross-sections. The novel sample tubes discussed here present signal improvements through both simulation and experiments, which were validated through power saturation experiments. The sample tube development methodology presented here provide a general framework for designing and implementing 3D printed EPR sample holders, based on resonator electromagnetic field distribution and dielectric properties of the photopolymer material.

papers.title: Filament assembly confers the mechanical resilience of the IFI16 restrictosome
papers.abstract: Interferon-inducible protein 16 (IFI16) is a mammalian innate immune sensor composed of a filament-forming pyrin domain (PYD) followed by tandem HIN200 domains that bind nucleic acids. First recognized as a major regulator of inflammatory responses against cytosolic double-stranded (ds)DNA, IFI16 filaments have been implicated in several key mechanical processes involving both host and pathogens, including viral replication restriction, latency regulation, replication-stress responses, and DNA-damage responses. Moreover, IFI16 filaments are ultra-stable, a key trait believed to drive its autoantigenicity. Although recent studies reported that IFI16 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) via disordered linkers and multivalent protein-dsDNA interactions, whether such a metastable entity provides a framework for the mechanical activities of IFI16 remains unknown. Here, we show that PYD-driven filament assembly confers the mechanical stability of IFI16 condensates by compacting DNA into ultra-stable tangles capable of withstanding forces sufficient to induce duplex deformation. By contrast, HIN200-dsDNA complexes are much more sensitive to ionic perturbation, DNA pretension, and mechanical interference. Together, we demonstrate that filament assembly allows IFI16 to act as a mechano-sensitive restrictor.

papers.title: Single Molecule Diffusion Studies Reveal Rapid Translations Across Target Membrane Surfaces for both p40Phox PX domain and Class III PI3K VPS34 Complex 1, the Autophagy Lipid Kinase
papers.abstract: Single molecule analyses are providing new insights into the molecular mechanisms by which peripheral membrane proteins approach and translate across a target bilayer surface before stable docking. Here we compare and contrast the translational movements of four diffusers on a representative supported lipid bilayer: (i) the fluorescent lipid LRB-(DO)PE, (ii) the G-protein Rab1A anchored to (DO)PE; (iii) the PI(3)P sensor p40Phox PX domain, and (iv) the autophagy lipid kinase VPS34 Complex 1. The latter enzyme is a Class III PI-3-Kinase and its unusual architecture exhibits two distinct membrane-docking "feet" unique to Class III PI3Ks. Notably, the membrane contact surfaces of the PX domain and autophagy lipid kinase each possess multiple positive charges suitable for electrostatic interactions with their anionic target membrane. The present single molecule tracking studies reveal that both the fluorescent lipid and the lipid-anchored G protein Rab1A exhibit 2-dimensional translation typical of simple lipid diffusion in the bilayer. Single molecule density measurements indicate both PX domain and autophagy lipid kinase exhibit significantly reduced membrane docking when the bilayer negative charge is decreased, confirming the importance of their protein-bilayer electrostatic interactions. Single molecule tracking studies reveal that both PX domain and autophagy lipid kinase exhibit hopping movements across the bilayer surface during their initial bilayer contacts, yielding a significantly higher frequency of long range displacements than allowed by lipid 2-D diffusion. After transitioning from hopping to a stable bilayer-docked state, both PX domain and autophagy lipid kinase exhibit 2-D diffusion slower than lipid diffusion indicating the appearance of increased frictional drag against the bilayer due to new protein-bilayer contacts. PX domain requires its target lipid for the transition from electrostatic hopping to stable bilayer docking, while autophagy lipid kinase can dock spontaneously to anionic lipid bilayers even in the absence of its substrate lipid. In principle, the slowly diffusing, bilayer-docked states of PX domain and autophagy lipid kinase could be interrupted by unbinding-hopping-rebinding events. However, such events are not detected for PX domain in the presence of target lipid (DO)PI(3)P nor for autophagy lipid kinase in the presence of substrate lipid (DO)PI. Instead, unbinding-hopping-rebinding events are only observed for autophagy lipid kinase in the absence of substrate lipid, indicating that the presence of a specific binding lipid reduces the frequency or spatial amplitude of such events. Overall, the findings provide evidence that p40Phox PX domain possesses a search mechanism involving electrostatic hopping that speeds its acquisition of target lipid, as previously observed for PH domains. The evidence indicates that the autophagy lipid kinase also exhibits electrostatic hopping/skating behavior that is proposed to play a functional role by speeding regulatory encounters with autophagy lipid kinase activators and effectors. Moreover, the ability of the lipid kinase to spontaneously dock to anionic membranes without a target lipid could facilitate its distribution across broad regions of the growing autophagosome. Finally, the autophagy lipid kinase exhibits multiple translational modes that we hypothesize are enabled by its two membrane docking feet.

papers.title: Inferring scaling laws of branching networks from their geometry by global optimization
papers.abstract: Optimality principles are widely used to understand branching networks, yet they are tested on individual branchings that cannot reliably distinguish competing scaling laws. We formulate the missing link between the laws and measurements by mapping each law to its predicted branch points through global optimization. Vascular branch points closely match weighted-length optima when each vessel is allowed its own fitted weight. Inferred scaling laws reveal type-specific geometric signatures hidden from local analysis. They beat all tested laws, including Murray's law in 1,679 of 1,744 held-out hepatic and pulmonary trees. For coronary arteries on the heart surface, an exact discrete optimization model extends the framework beyond convex geometry and supports area-preserving scaling. The framework also identifies distinct laws for airways and plant shoots while rejecting weighted-length optimality for neuronal axons. Global optimization turns network geometry into a quantitative test of the principles that govern branching networks.

papers.title: Low-pass filtering revisited: ramped phase randomization for cryo-EM map comparison and data augmentation
papers.abstract: Conventional low-pass filters attenuate or remove high-frequency Fourier amplitudes but leave the phases intact wherever the amplitude response stays above zero. As a result, fine-scale detail of the original signal can persist beyond the target resolution. A sharp cutoff removes this detail but produces ringing artifacts. To address both limitations, this work introduces ramped phase randomization, which extends a conventional low-pass filter by adding random offsets to Fourier phases that increase smoothly with spatial frequency. For cryo-EM maps, the correlation between a map at the target resolution and an ideal, noiseless map sets the levels of the phase offsets, with a correction for the finite resolution of the input map. On three published map pairs, ramped phase filtering reduced the higher resolution parent's fine detail to a level similar to that of independently determined maps at the lower target resolution, whereas amplitude-only filtering kept the parent's sharp features. The FSCs between the filtered maps and their parents closely resembled those of the experimental maps. The same filter also serves as a data augmentation approach for neural network-based machine learning. With ramped phase randomization, each augmented copy keeps the power spectrum and low-frequency content of the original example but has a different high-frequency pattern. For simulated CryoBench particles of 16 ribosome assembly states, phase augmentation raised mean test accuracy in all 20 combinations of training-set size and latent dimension, by 20.8 percentage points on average (range from 3.3 points to 44.2 points). On two general deep learning benchmarks, mean test accuracy rose from 92.15% to 96.99% with 60 labelled UCI Synthetic Control traces and from 53.44% to 74.27% with 500 labelled noisy MNIST images. The ramped phase randomization is implemented in an open-source Python package, with a companion browser application for interactive visualization of cryo-EM maps and filtering effects.

papers.title: Kinetic gating by an iron sulfur chain modulates flavin radical-pair spin chemistry in mitochondrial Complex I
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial Complex I generates reactive oxygen species at its flavin cofactor, where spin dependent reaction pathways have been proposed. Models of this chemistry treat the flavin oxygen radical pair in isolation, although the flavin is wired to a chain of eight iron sulfur clusters. Here we model the pair with this chain using the human Complex I structure and open quantum system models of spin coupling and electron transfer. In the simulated network, spin coherence decays rapidly along the chain, whereas proximal clusters alter the calculated radical-pair singlet yield. Their influence is kinetically gated: a downstream cluster affects the modelled yield when its electron-transfer rate competes with radical pair recombination, a threshold robust to driving force and to the transfer model. Modelling does set the sign: one directional spin hops predict suppression and inflate coherence transport, whereas charge resolved transfer drives the singlet yield towards its spin-randomized limit unless triplet recombination dominates. Detectable spin dependent effects in this framework require superoxide spin relaxation to be substantially slower than in free solution, a condition not yet established for Complex I.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic flow in the gut hinders the fixation of beneficial mutants but accelerates their invasion
papers.abstract: Gut bacteria experience a spatially structured environment with hydrodynamic flow. Using a branching-process approach, we show that beneficial mutants arising randomly upon division have a reduced fixation probability compared to the well-mixed case. The suppression factor is set by the spatial heterogeneity of mutant fate across the gut. In contrast, the invasion of mutant lineages that avoid early stochastic extinction is accelerated in the gut compared to a matched well-mixed case. Stronger advective flow decreases fixation probabilities while accelerating mutant invasion.

papers.title: Osmotic Coupling of Mechanics and Epigenetics Regulates Chromatin Phase Organization
papers.abstract: Cells experience epigenetic, osmotic, and mechanical perturbations that reorganize chromatin, yet how these distinct cues are integrated into a common physical response of the nucleus remains unclear. Here, we identify nuclear hydration as a central state variable that links microenvironmental perturbations to chromatin phase organization and nuclear mechanics. We develop a non-equilibrium mesoscale model that couples chromatin elasticity, water transport, and epigenetic reaction-diffusion kinetics. In this framework, chromatin behaves as a deformable polymer that segregates into coexisting water-rich euchromatic and water-poor heterochromatic phases, whose compositions and morphologies are regulated by hydration-dependent swelling, elastic strain, and histone-mark interconversion. The model predicts that epigenetic perturbations, osmotic shocks, and volume-changing mechanical loads reorganize chromatin by shifting intranuclear water content, nuclear volume, and euchromatin-heterochromatin phase balance. It further predicts that anisotropic forces impose directional strain, driving heterochromatin elongation, alignment, and lamellar transitions. Quantitative comparisons with super-resolution imaging, AFM and chromatin-accessibility measurement - across pharmacological, osmotic, and mechanical perturbations including confinement and micropatterning - support these predictions. Together, our results establish a chemo-mechano-osmotic framework in which nuclear hydration integrates biochemical and biophysical cues to regulate chromatin organization across scales.

papers.title: Lipopolysaccharide chain length and coat assembly keep guanylate-binding proteins upright on bacterial membranes
papers.abstract: Guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) defend host cells by assembling on intracellular pathogen membranes. For human GBP1, this requires a switch from a compact, closed conformation to an extended, open one, whereas for murine orthologues the open state is not known. How the open state behaves at a membrane has remained inaccessible to experiment. Using all-atom and coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations covering over 0.5 ms, we followed human GBP1 and murine GBP2 as monomers, dimers, and higher-order assemblies on phosphatidylcholine membranes, Shigella flexneri lipopolysaccharide (LPS), and phosphoinositide-containing bilayers. Closed GBPs dock through their prenyl anchor with minimal lipid selectivity. Open GBPs, by contrast, are intrinsically unstable: monomers fold back into membrane-bound resting states, and dimers tip over unless supported, either by long LPS O-antigen chains or by neighboring molecules within a coat. The open state thus appears to be maintained not by the nucleotide alone but by the protein's molecular environment.

papers.title: Opposing Regulation of Tau Condensation by Phosphorylation Levels and Molecular Chaperone Interactions
papers.abstract: Aggregation of the microtubule-stabilizing protein Tau into insoluble deposits is characteristic for several neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease. While phosphorylated Tau (pTau) appears as a normal post-translational modification, the accumulation of hyperphosphorylated Tau aggregates represents a hallmark of these disorders. The molecular mechanisms involved in the conversion from functional Tau into pathological assemblies are still not elucidated. Here, we identified the role of phosphorylation levels on the phase separation and aggregation behavior of Tau, and how these processes can be counteracted by the molecular chaperone-like Bri2 BRICHOS domain. We found that the phosphorylation pattern modulates Tau fibrillation and enhances its droplet-formation propensity. Remarkably, Bri2 BRICHOS generally shifts Tau phase boundaries, counteracting the dense state, and inhibits Tau fibril formation, irrespectively of the degree of phosphorylation. Solution NMR results pinpointed the binding site of Bri2 BRICHOS on pTau, both in the dilute phase and droplet state, revealing an effect on specific regions and phosphorylated residues, which appear to be crucial for the formation and maintenance of the droplet state. Taken together, this study uncovered the opposing regulatory roles of phosphorylation and the anti-amyloid chaperone Bri2 BRICHOS on biomolecular condensation and fibrillation of Tau, providing detailed insights into the molecular mechanisms involved in tauopathies, which may facilitate future treatment strategies using chaperone-based inhibitors.

papers.title: Mass spectrometric detection of protein nanoclusters: the invisible intermediates of phase separation
papers.abstract: Phase separation of biomolecules, including intrinsically disordered proteins, is an underlying physical process behind cellular condensate formation. To increase mechanistic understanding of its initial stages, we demonstrate the application of charge detection mass spectrometry to characterise the mass dispersion of protein nanoclusters that represent intermediates in this important biophysical process. We detect polydisperse clusters of 1-280 protein molecules (64 kDa-18.4 MDa), that are currently invisible to most analytical techniques.

papers.title: Oxygen drives a rapid, reversible photoprotective switch in photosynthetic antennae
papers.abstract: Oxygen is the archetypal agent of photooxidative damage, and it is generally countered by removing its reactive products or by regulated, energy-costly responses. We show that in photosynthetic light-harvesting complexes, oxygen also drives a rapid, reversible photoprotective switch. Using a new bulk fluorescence method that separates reversible dark states from irreversible photobleaching, together with single-molecule spectroscopy, we find that illumination and oxygen generate a reversible, protein-stabilized charge-separated state comprising oxidized chlorophyll and superoxide. Access to this state increasingly outcompetes irreversible photodamage as excitation intensity falls to physiological levels and is strongly accelerated by ascorbic acid in native thylakoid membranes. These findings identify a constitutive oxygen-dependent photoprotective pathway and suggest that redox-state recovery can determine whether oxygen-associated chemistry protects or damages photoactive systems.

papers.title: RhoA effectors ROCK and SLK/LOK oppositely regulate VE-cadherin mobility at endothelial junctions
papers.abstract: Cellular contractile forces regulate VE-cadherin dynamics, adhesion, and endothelial junction integrity. RhoA controls these forces through two parallel effector kinases: ROCK, which activates non-muscle myosin II motors, and SLK/LOK, which promote actin-membrane attachment through phosphorylation of ezrin, radixin, moesin proteins (ERM). How these two RhoA effector pathways differentially affect VE-cadherin dynamics at junctions is not known. Using single-molecule tracking of Halo-tagged VE-cadherin, we obtained a detailed characterization of VE-cadherin diffusive behavior inside and outside junctional regions in cultured human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC). VE-cadherin was substantially less mobile and more confined within junctions than in non-junctional membrane. Inhibiting ROCK with Y-27632 increased VE-cadherin mobility both inside and outside junctions, consistent with RhoA/ROCK-driven contractility restraining cadherin diffusion globally. Unexpectedly, inhibiting SLK/LOK produced the opposite effect, selectively reducing VE-cadherin mobility within junctions with no comparable change outside them. This effect was accompanied by an increase in reticular junctions, suggesting that SLK/LOK inhibition alters VE-cadherin mobility indirectly, through a change in junctional architecture, rather than through a direct effect of actin-membrane coupling on VE-cadherin itself. These findings identify SLK/LOK as a regulator of VE-cadherin dynamics acting in parallel to ROCK downstream of RhoA and point to junctional architecture as a previously unappreciated determinant of VE-cadherin mobility at endothelial cell-cell contacts.

papers.title: Extreme Slowdown of dsDNA and RNA:DNA Hybrids in Solid-state Nanopores for LiCl concentrations above 4 mol/L
papers.abstract: Solid-state nanopores enable single-molecule detection and characterization through ionic-current measurements, but rapid translocation can limit the resolution of molecular features. Here, we investigated the translocation of 7.2 kb dsDNA and 3.3 kb RNA:DNA hybrids at LiCl concentrations extending to 7 mol/L. Both constructs exhibited a substantial increase of {gtrsim} 500% in mean translocation time when increasing LiCl concentration from 2--3 M to 7 M . We also observed a decrease in translocation frequency at increasing LiCl concentration. Both observations indicate a reduction in the effective electric driving force. Further analysis indicates a substantial decrease in the relative width of secondary peaks induced by labels on the molecule. Our results show that increasing salt concentration beyond 4 mol/L is an accessible way for increasing translocation time in solid-state nanopore sensing, with possible implications for barcode sensing resolution.

papers.title: RBC Deformability During Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Treatment
papers.abstract: Philadelphia chromosome positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL) is the most common genetic subgroup in adult ALL, and its incidence increases with age. In this longitudinal single-subject study, we investigate erythrocyte deformability as a disease-associated biomechanical marker in parallel with clinical, hematological, and molecular response throughout the treatment process in a 75-year-old patient diagnosed with Ph+ ALL. Using optical tweezers, we performed high-resolution single-cell mechanical stretching experiments to quantify the deformability of individual RBCs obtained from the patient and a healthy control. Our measurements reveal a pronounced relation between state of diseases/therapy and RBC deformability in the ALL patient, indicating systemic alterations in cellular biomechanics associated with leukemic pathophysiology. These findings suggest that changes in RBC mechanical properties, probed through non-invasive optical tweezers-based techniques, may accompany disease presence and progression.

papers.title: Correlation-resolved sum-frequency generation microscopy of biological tissue with bright twin beams
papers.abstract: Sum-frequency generation (SFG) driven by bright twin beams generated through high-gain parametric down-conversion comprises a coherent component arising from correlated mode pairs and an incoherent component arising from interactions between uncorrelated modes. Modal correlations can enhance coherent SFG in anisotropic nonlinear media, for example by extending the effective interaction length. Whether such correlations can likewise benefit image formation in heterogeneous biological tissue remains unknown. Here we address this question by performing SFG imaging of biological tissue using bright twin beams as the excitation source. Spectral decomposition of the SFG signal separates its coherent and incoherent components, allowing us to reconstruct co-registered images and examine how twin-beam correlations influence image formation. In mouse skeletal muscle, the coherent-component image revealed sarcomere periodicity with a Bragg-spot-to-background ratio of approximately 310, compared with 7.5 in the incoherent-component image. In fresh human dermis, the coherent-component image showed greater Fourier power than the incoherent-component image in the 0.30-0.50 mu m^{-1} band and a greater fractional autocovariance decay at short spatial lags. These results demonstrate that twin-beam correlations can enhance contrast and detectability at selected spatial frequencies in heterogeneous tissue. Correlation-resolved SFG microscopy thus offers a route for exploiting bright quantum-light sources in nonlinear optical bioimaging.

papers.title: Room-temperature light-state structure of the AsLOV2-Rac1 optogenetic actuator by sheet-on-sheet serial femtosecond crystallography
papers.abstract: Light-oxygen-voltage (LOV) domains are blue-light sensors that make fused effector proteins optically controllable. The AsLOV2-Rac1 fusion (PA-Rac1) is one of the most widely used of these tools, yet the structural basis of its activation has been inferred largely from cryogenic structures and from solution studies, mostly of the isolated AsLOV2 domain. Here, room-temperature dark and light-state structures of AsLOV2-Rac1 at 1.8 [A] resolution are reported, determined by serial femtosecond crystallography at the SwissFEL Cristallina beamline with sheet-on-sheet (SOS) chip sample delivery. Repeated 450 nm pump-laser excitation during chip rastering accumulated the FMN-cysteine adduct in about 80 % of the molecules, giving strong Fourier difference maps. To our knowledge, this is the first light-state structure of PA-Rac1 or of any AsLOV2 fusion and the first AsLOV2 light state in which the thioether adduct is not compromised by X-ray radiolysis. Apart from the N-terminal residue and one marginal Rac1 loop residue, C displacements above 0.3 [A] between dark and light models recorded at the same temperature are confined to the chromophore environment, the D helix and the G{beta}-H{beta} and H{beta}-I{beta} loops of AsLOV2. These changes, including the Ile445 rotamer switch, are also seen in light-state structures of the isolated AsLOV2 domain, but the Asn414 rotation reported there is absent in the fusion. Comparison with the cryogenic dark-state structure also shows temperature-dependent differences that exaggerate the apparent changes. In the crystal, the GTP, the Mg2+ site and the switch regions of Rac1 show no detectable light-induced change and the J helix does not unfold, although transient or low-population states cannot be excluded. This modest response is consistent with the small difference in effector affinity between dark- and lit-state mutants in solution, with lattice contacts and an interdomain Ca2+ ion as possible further contributions.

papers.title: Semidilute Polymer Scaling Controls PEG-induced Protein Phase Separation
papers.abstract: When does polyethylene glycol (PEG) mass concentration provide a common measure of crowding strength across polymer chain lengths? Here we use bovine serum albumin (BSA) and PEG as a controlled depletion system and measure both coexisting phases to determine binodals, tie lines, and critical points across PEG molecular weights of 4--100 kDa. Phase diagrams for PEG 20, 35, and 100 kDa approximately collapse in mass-concentration coordinates, consistent with semidilute polymer scaling. Generalized free volume theory (GFVT) describes the BSA binodals and tie lines. It also approximately describes binodals for three additional globular proteins in PEG 35K, extending the comparison across proteins spanning 7.2--66.4 kDa. For the binary PEG mixtures tested, GFVT approximates the binodals using an effective polymer size corresponding to the weight-average molecular weight. These results identify a regime in which PEG mass concentration (g/L) provides a transferable measure of depletion-induced crowding.

papers.title: Mechanoadaptive focal adhesion-actomyosin coupling organizes diverse modes across ECM stiffness
papers.abstract: Focal adhesions mechanically couple the actomyosin cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix (ECM), contributing to mechanosensing and mechanical homeostasis. They span diverse states in response to the mechanical environment, from nascent adhesions and focal complexes to mature and supermature adhesions, undergoing dynamic remodeling. However, how ECM-dependent force generation and internal mechanoadaptation jointly shape the emergence and stability of these states remains unclear. Here, we develop a four-variable dynamical model comprising adhesion state, transmitted force, reinforcement activity, and an adaptive mechanical stress target. As ECM stiffness varies, the model generates distinct modes while regulating mechanical stress toward this target. The force-response timescale further modifies the stability structure, giving rise to a stable oscillatory mode. Within multistable regimes, adhesion-mode selection depends not only on current ECM stiffness but also on its history. These results show that diverse adhesion modes can emerge from a common mechanoadaptive system, with ECM stiffness history influencing mode selection.

papers.title: PHENOMS: Open-Source Software for Rust-Accelerated Hydrogen-Bond Analysis in Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: Hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) provides powerful insight into protein structure and dynamics, but interpretation of protection patterns at atomic resolution often requires complementary computational modeling. We present PHENOMS, an open-source Python package that integrates molecular dynamics trajectories with HDX-MS data to analyze backbone hydrogen-bond networks by tracking how individual hydrogen bonds and residue-residue contacts form, break, and reorganize throughout the simulations. This residue-level analysis can reveal local structural changes that may be missed by conventional global trajectory metrics. PHENOMS employs a multithreaded, Rust-accelerated computational engine that achieved an average 16-fold speedup (up to 100-fold) over widely used Python-based MD analysis packages in our benchmarks, while retaining individual hydrogen-bond resolution in every trajectory frame. We demonstrate PHENOMS through multiple retrospective case studies using published and in-house datasets, showing that it can recapitulate HDX-MS protection patterns, identify key residues that drive coordinated structural changes, and benchmark the computational efficiency of the approach. With automated quality-control workflows, PHENOMS provides a framework for integrating hydrogen-bond analysis with HDX-MS data or serves as a standalone, high-throughput tool for analyzing MD trajectories for broader applications in protein engineering, drug discovery, and structural biology.

papers.title: Interpretable Deep Learning of Endogenous Fluorophore Concentration and Entropy for Lung Tissue Classification
papers.abstract: Fluorophore concentration measures and local histogram entropy describe different aspects of endogenous fluorophore maps. We investigate whether their combination improves discrimination between normal and cancerous lung tissue and which features contribute to predictions. Chemometric fluorescence microscopy (CFM) provides concentration maps of tryptophan, elastin, reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH), and flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD). A neural network based on generalized additive models with structured interactions (GAMI-Net) is used to compare concentration-only, entropy-only, and combined representations through explicit main effects and pairwise interactions. The mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC AUCs) across five-fold cross-validation were $95.9% pm 0.7%$, $96.4% pm 1.6%$, and $98.4% pm 0.7%$, respectively; variability is reported as standard deviation (SD). Their aggregate differences are consistent with the hypothesis of complementary predictive information. FAD entropy, NADH concentration, and NADH entropy were the leading main effects in the combined model. The learned log-odds contributions include a U-shaped elastin-entropy relationship and nonmonotonic tryptophan relationships. By exposing how concentration and entropy enter predictions, this interpretable framework turns label-free fluorescence classification into specific, testable hypotheses about tissue metabolism and extracellular-matrix organization, motivating specimen-grouped and external validation.

papers.title: Polarization affects viscoelasticity and podosome distribution of primary human macrophages
papers.abstract: Macrophages are essential cells of the innate immune system that regulate wound healing and tissue homeostasis. They exert diverse functions, depending on their polarization state, which can lead to either functional healing of the tissue or fibrosis. Macrophage polarization state is affected by both the local biochemical and mechanical microenvironment within the tissue, suggesting a possible dependence of macrophage function on cell mechanical state, which has been poorly explored to date. In this study, we provide a systematic and quantitative characterization of the viscoelastic properties of unstimulated, pro-inflammatory, and anti-inflammatory monocyte-derived primary human macrophages at the single-cell level using atomic force microscopy. Pro-inflammatory macrophages exhibited a lower elastic modulus (E = 458.8 {+/-} 179.9 Pa) and a more dissipative response (low frequency exponent = 0.22 {+/-} 0.03) than anti-inflammatory macrophages (E = 716 {+/-} 345.6 Pa and = 0.15 {+/-} 0.04). These differences in mechanical properties were independent of cell morphology but correlated with differences in podosome distribution with pro-inflammatory macrophages exhibiting a dispersed distribution, and anti-inflammatory macrophages a more clustered distribution. This study identifies polarization-dependent mechanical differences in human primary macrophages and provides a quantitative experimental framework for future work in macrophage mechanobiology.

papers.title: Injector-based pump-probe serial synchrotron crystallography of CrPhotLOV1 at the MicroMAX beamline
papers.abstract: Time-resolved serial synchrotron crystallography (TR-SSX) has become a powerful approach for investigating structural dynamics in proteins under near-physiological conditions. Its successful application, however, depends on robust sample delivery, reliable pump-probe synchronization, and reproducible data-processing strategies. Here, an injector-based pump-probe TR-SSX workflow at the MicroMAX beamline is applied to investigate the structural dynamics of the LOV1 domain of the blue-light photoreceptor phototropin from Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (CrPhotLOV1). Room-temperature serial datasets were collected for an independently measured laser-off dark state together with four light-activated pump-probe time windows (0-350, 500-850, 1000-1350 and 1500-1850 {micro}s after a microsecond laser pulse). All four time windows and an interleaved pump-probe dark reference were recorded in a single run with the JUNGFRAU detector at 2 kHz. Because thioether adduct formation in CrPhotLOV1 is complete within about 20 {micro}s and the adduct persists for hundreds of seconds, the four delays probe the same photoadduct state and serve as independent replicates. The workflow was evaluated in terms of data quality, light contamination in the pump-probe dark reference, difference Fourier analysis, extrapolated electron-density maps and refinement of light-state models. Consistent activation levels were obtained across all time points, enabling reliable structural interpretation of the light-activated state. Difference Fourier maps and refined extrapolated models reproducibly revealed formation of the characteristic FMN-Cys57 thioether adduct together with localized rearrangements within the chromophore-binding pocket. The refined light-state structures agree closely with previously reported CrPhotLOV1 models. These results establish a robust and reproducible workflow for injector-based pump-probe TR-SSX at the MicroMAX beamline, suitable for routine time-resolved studies of light-responsive proteins.
